quote: Naturally, one may wonder whether the following statement is actually also true: For 0 < β ≤ 1, (α_1, . . . , α_n) ⪯^p (α_1^*, . . . , α_n^*) gives rise to the usual stochastic order between X_{1:n} and X_{1:n}^*. The following example gives negative answer to these two conjecture. Example 3. Let (X_1, X_2) ((X_1^*, X_2^*)) be a vector of independent heterogeneous GMW random variables. Set β = 0.5, γ = 2 and λ = 3. For (α_1, α_2) = (2, 3) ⪯^p (1, 5.5) = (α_1^*, α_2^*), X_{1:2} ≥_st X_{1:2}^*, as can be seen in Fig. 3 (A); however, for (α_1, α_2) = (1.1, 6) ⪯^p (1, 2.25) = (α_1^*, α_2^*), X_{1:2} ≤_st X_{1:2}^*, as can be seen in Fig. 3 (B) So, (α_1, α_2) ⪯^p (α_1^*, α_2^*) implies neither X_{1:2} ≤_st X_{1:2}^* nor X_{1:2} ≥_st X_{1:2}^* for 0 < β ≤ 1.

quote: We say that random variable X belongs to the Exponentiated Scale (ES) family of distributions if X ∼ H(x) = [G(λx)]^α, where α, λ > 0 and G is called the baseline distribution function which we assume that is absolutely continuous. In the sequel, we denote this family by ES(α, λ). Bashkar et al. (2017) proved the following general result. Theorem 11. Suppose for i = 1, ..., n, X_i ∼ ES(α_i, λ) and X_i^* ∼ ES(α_i^*, λ) share a common Archimedean survival copula with generator ϕ. Then, X_{1:n} ≤_st X_{1:n}^* if (α_1, . . . , α_n) ⪰^w (α_1^*, . . . , α_n^*).
family: Exponentiated scale ES(α, λ): H(x) = [G(λx)]^α, α, λ > 0, G an absolutely continuous baseline cdf (arbitrary); common λ; α_i heterogeneous; dependent components with a common Archimedean survival copula (generator ϕ)

quote: In the sequel, by X ∼ GMW(β, α, γ, λ, ϕ) we mean that X has the Archimedean copula with generator ϕ and for i = 1, ..., n, X_i ∼ GMW(β_i, α, γ, λ). The smallest order statistic X_{1:n} of the sample X ∼ GMW(β, α, γ, λ, ϕ) has the survival function Ḡ_{X_{1:n}}(x) = ϕ(Σ_{i=1}^{n} ψ(1 − (F(α, γ, λ, x))^{β_i})) ≡ J(β, α, γ, λ, x, ϕ) (8) where, F(α, γ, λ, x) = 1 − exp(−αx^γ exp(λx)). Theorem 13. For X ∼ GMW(β, α, γ, λ, ϕ_1) and X^* ∼ GMW(β^*, α, γ, λ, ϕ_2), if ψ_2 ◦ ϕ_1 is super-additive, then (β_1, . . . , β_n) ⪰^w (β_1^*, . . . , β_n^*) implies X_{1:n} ≤_st X_{1:n}^*.

quote: In the ES family, Bashkar et al. (2018) obtained some sufficient conditions for the comparison of parallel systems under some well-known stochastic orderings.
